approvalRequirements: Be an active Shakopee Public Utilities residential electric or water customer for the applicable measure.
Purchase and install a new residential product or system that meets the current ENERGY STAR or program efficiency specifications.
Use the measure-specific electric or water rebate pathway and satisfy any service, installation, and quantity limits.
Submit the current rebate claim with the customer account, itemized receipt or invoice, model information, and other requested documentation by the applicable deadline.
Permit Shakopee Public Utilities to verify customer, product, and installation eligibility before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current 2026 residential program uses published, prescriptive eligibility and documentation rules. A qualifying residential claim is likely to be paid after review, but the supplied commercial dishwasher and commercial-refrigeration mappings are not supported by the residential offering.
reviews.evidenceText: Shakopee Public Utilities currently lists 2026 residential rebates for qualifying appliances, LED lighting, central cooling, air-source and ground-source heat pumps, and related household measures, with account and claim documentation requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible South Hadley Electric Light Department customer with the charger installed at an eligible service address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying connected Level 2 charger and meet the program equipment and connectivity requirements.
Use a licensed electrician, obtain required permits, and complete the applicable electrical inspection.
Enroll the charger in the current scheduled-charging or Connected Homes pathway and complete the required participation term.
Submit the rebate application with proof of purchase, equipment, account, installation, and participation documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current charger rebate follows objective customer, equipment, installation, enrollment, and participation rules rather than competitive selection. A compliant participant is likely to receive the rebate after the required term and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: SHELD currently offers qualifying connected-charger incentives tied to permitted installation, program enrollment, scheduled-charging participation, and submission of purchase and device records.

approvalRequirements: Use an eligible commercial property in a Missouri municipality that participates in Show Me PACE.
Propose a permanent qualifying energy-efficiency or renewable-energy improvement with documented savings and a savings-to-investment ratio above the program minimum.
Provide the technical project proposal, costs, savings analysis, ownership, property, tax, and lien information required by the program and capital provider.
Obtain written consent from each existing mortgage lender.
Pass private capital-provider underwriting and program eligibility review, then execute the PACE assessment and financing documents before funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: C-PACE financing is not automatic: approval depends on municipality participation, project economics, mortgage-lender consent, property standing, private underwriting, and closing. The current official materials do not expressly confirm a standalone battery-storage project, so the supplied mapping needs project-specific confirmation.
reviews.evidenceText: Show Me PACE requires a participating Missouri jurisdiction, a qualifying permanent project with favorable economics, mortgage-lender consent, property and financial documentation, private capital underwriting, and program closing.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SELCO commercial, municipal, industrial, general-service customer, or other currently allowed applicant for the selected measure.
Propose a qualifying commercial heat-pump or electric-vehicle charging project meeting current equipment, networking, connector, demand-response, and site requirements as applicable.
Submit the measure-specific application before work with contractor quotes, equipment specifications, AHRI documentation for heat pumps, or site and electrical plans for charging equipment.
Receive written SELCO project approval before purchasing equipment, beginning construction, or installing the measure.
Complete required permits and inspections and submit final invoices, equipment records, and completion documentation for payment review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SELCO publishes defined preapproval and closeout paths for commercial heat pumps and EV charging. A conforming, preapproved project is likely to be paid after installation verification, although the broad high-efficiency-HVAC mapping should be limited to currently qualifying commercial heat-pump work.
reviews.evidenceText: Current SELCO commercial materials require advance project review for qualifying heat pumps and EV charging, followed by permits, inspections, invoices, and final verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SELCO residential electric customer and install the measure at the qualifying Shrewsbury service address.
Purchase and install equipment or complete weatherization work that meets the current NextZero measure specifications.
Use licensed or participating contractors and provide AHRI, model, efficiency, invoice, and installation records where required.
Complete a home assessment, recommended weatherization, post-installation inspection, or other measure-specific step when required for the selected incentive tier.
Submit the complete current application within the applicable purchase, installation, and filing period.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current NextZero offerings use objective residential equipment, assessment, inspection, and documentation rules. Qualifying claims are likely to be paid, but the supplied generic efficient-fan or blower mapping and broad HVAC category are not independently established by the current program pages.
reviews.evidenceText: Shrewsbury NextZero currently provides residential appliance, heat-pump, thermostat, water-heating, and weatherization incentives with measure-specific assessments, contractor records, inspections, and filing deadlines.

approvalRequirements: Be a Silicon Valley Power business customer with an eligible project at a Santa Clara service address.
Use the applicable prescriptive, electrification, or custom pathway and meet the current equipment and energy-savings specifications.
Have the customer register and submit the project application with signed forms, specifications, costs, and savings documentation.
Complete any required pre-installation inspection and obtain written Silicon Valley Power approval before purchasing or installing equipment.
Finish the approved project within the authorization period and submit invoices, closeout records, and access for post-installation inspection or savings verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current business program covers the principal mapped lighting, HVAC, water-heating, refrigeration, controls, and food-service measures through published prescriptive or reviewed custom pathways. A technically qualifying project that obtains advance approval and passes final verification is likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: Silicon Valley Power currently requires business customers to submit project details, complete pre-inspection and written approval when required, and provide final invoices and installation verification before rebate payment.

approvalRequirements: Be an active Silicon Valley Power residential customer and install the measure in an eligible existing residence served by the utility.
Purchase and install a new qualifying heat pump, heat-pump water heater, EV charger, laundry appliance, induction appliance, or other currently listed product.
Meet the current model, efficiency, installation, and permit requirements for the selected measure.
Submit the application with paid invoice, model and serial information, installation records, and permit proof when applicable.
File within the current measure deadline, generally including the program filing period after purchase or installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current residential electrification program provides prescriptive rebates under published customer, product, permit, and documentation rules. A complete claim for a qualifying existing-home installation is likely to be paid after administrative review.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Silicon Valley Power rules support qualifying existing-home heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, EV charging, laundry, and induction equipment and require timely claims with purchase, model, installation, and permit records.

approvalRequirements: Be a Singing River Electric member with an eligible residence in the cooperative service area.
Use the applicable new-home or existing-home conversion pathway and install a qualifying high-efficiency heat pump or geothermal system.
Meet the current efficiency and equipment-certification requirements, including applicable AHRI or ARI certification.
Provide the equipment, contractor, installation, and member information required by the Comfort Advantage process.
Complete any program verification or inspection required before the incentive is issued.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Comfort Advantage publishes defined member, equipment, efficiency, and conversion requirements rather than a competitive selection process. A qualifying documented installation is likely to receive the stated incentive after verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Singing River Electric currently describes Comfort Advantage incentives for qualifying high-efficiency heat-pump and geothermal installations, including equipment-certification and program-verification requirements.

approvalRequirements: When a funding round is open, be a Pennsylvania small business with no more than the program employee limit and an eligible in-state project.
Propose an eligible energy-efficiency or pollution-prevention project that meets the minimum cost-savings or resource-reduction threshold.
Submit the online application, calculations, contractor quotes, project budget, and business documentation before the round closes.
Do not begin disallowed work before the applicable program start date and complete the project within the award period.
Submit completion, invoice, payment, and performance documentation for reimbursement after award.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The official 2025-2026 application period closed on March 13, 2026, and the project-completion date was June 30, 2026. No later open round was verified as of the audit date, so a new application is unlikely to receive an award unless Pennsylvania announces another cycle.
reviews.evidenceText: Pennsylvania states that the 2025-2026 Small Business Advantage Grant round closed March 13, 2026 and required awarded work to be completed by June 30, 2026.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Silicon Valley Power small-business customer in Santa Clara.
Request or accept the no-cost energy survey and provide reasonable site and operating information for the assessment.
Select a currently qualifying electric-efficiency project identified through the service or otherwise accepted by the utility.
Obtain Silicon Valley Power project preapproval before purchasing or installing the proposed measures.
Complete the approved work and submit invoices, completion records, and access for final verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current service provides a defined survey and project-support path, but the supplied opportunity maps only to a low-flow water fixture, which is not supported by the current electric-efficiency materials reviewed. An award is possible for a qualifying efficiency project, not established for that mapped measure.
reviews.evidenceText: Silicon Valley Power offers small businesses a no-cost energy survey, project assistance, enhanced qualifying rebates, and preapproval-based implementation support for electric-efficiency measures such as lighting, HVAC, controls, and food-service equipment.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Efficiency Maine small-business customer in the applicable utility rate or demand class.
Use the loan for a currently eligible heat-pump or variable-refrigerant-flow retrofit completed through a Qualified Partner.
Apply for and pass lender prequalification for an amount within the current program range.
Submit the project proposal, utility information, and required records for Efficiency Maine project preapproval.
Sign the approved work scope and loan documents before installation and submit the completion form after the project is finished.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program has a defined project pathway, but financing depends on both lender underwriting and Efficiency Maine project approval. A technically eligible retrofit therefore has a possible, not automatic, funding outcome.
reviews.evidenceText: Efficiency Maine currently offers small-business heat-pump and variable-refrigerant-flow loans through Qualified Partners, with lender prequalification, program project approval, signed loan documents, and completion confirmation.

approvalRequirements: Be a Pennsylvania small business with no more than the program employee limit at the project site.
Use the financing for an eligible project that reduces energy use, pollution, or waste and satisfies the current cost and payback rules.
Submit the technical eligibility application and supporting project, savings, cost, and business information to the Department of Environmental Protection.
Receive the Department of Environmental Protection technical approval letter.
Submit the financial application to the Department of Community and Economic Development and pass credit, repayment, collateral, and closing review.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The loan requires separate technical eligibility approval and borrower-specific financial underwriting. Eligible energy projects can be financed, but approval is not assured solely because the proposed equipment qualifies.
reviews.evidenceText: Pennsylvania currently administers the PPAA loan through Department of Environmental Protection technical approval followed by Department of Community and Economic Development financial review and loan closing.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Jersey customer proposing a qualifying combined-heat-and-power or fuel-cell project at an eligible site.
Meet the current technology, system-size, efficiency, fuel, interconnection, cost, and program requirements.
Submit the technical and financial application with equipment, engineering, cost, energy-use, savings, and project-development documentation before installation.
Receive program approval and an incentive commitment before purchasing or constructing the project.
Complete the project, satisfy commissioning and performance milestones, and submit invoices, inspection, and verification records before each payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: CHP and fuel-cell projects receive project-specific technical and financial review before commitment and milestone payments. Current official materials substantiate CHP and fuel cells, but not a standalone biomass or biogas system unless it is part of a qualifying CHP configuration.
reviews.evidenceText: New Jersey currently accepts applications for technically reviewed CHP and fuel-cell incentives that require advance commitment and project, commissioning, inspection, and performance documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Rhode Island homeowner or microbusiness using a qualifying project and installer under the current Renewable Energy Fund rules.
Propose an eligible net-metered photovoltaic or solar domestic hot-water system; claim a storage adder only with a qualifying concurrent renewable-energy award.
Have the selected installer submit the complete application during an open 2026 funding round with design, cost, ownership, technical, and interconnection information.
Receive a Commerce Rhode Island award letter and execute the grant agreement before installation begins.
Complete installation and interconnection and submit final invoices, completion records, and access for quality-assurance inspection before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The 2026 program uses limited funding rounds and requires formal selection, an award letter, and a grant agreement before construction. Solar photovoltaic, solar hot-water, and qualifying storage adders are supported, but an energy audit is preparatory rather than a separately funded retrofit.
reviews.evidenceText: Commerce Rhode Island lists multiple 2026 small-scale funding rounds and requires installer application, award documents before installation, interconnection, completion records, and quality-assurance review. Current materials cover solar photovoltaic, solar hot water, and a concurrent storage adder.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SMECO non-residential customer with an active account at the project site.
Propose a qualifying prescriptive or custom lighting, HVAC, refrigeration, controls, or other electric-efficiency project.
Submit the project application with equipment, cost, operating, and savings information before purchasing or installing equipment.
Receive SMECO preapproval before committing to the project.
Complete the approved scope and submit final invoices, specifications, completion records, and access for inspection or savings verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SMECO currently offers prescriptive and custom business incentives under a mandatory advance-approval process. A qualifying project that receives preapproval and submits complete closeout records is likely to be paid, subject to program limits and funding.
reviews.evidenceText: SMECO requires business projects to obtain approval before equipment purchase or installation and supports current lighting, HVAC, refrigeration, and custom efficiency pathways followed by final documentation and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SMECO residential customer or member with the measure installed at a qualifying service address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying HVAC system, heat-pump water heater, smart thermostat, appliance, or connected-control measure.
Use an authorized contractor, distributor, retailer, or program enrollment route when required for the selected incentive.
Meet current model, efficiency, installation, connectivity, and participation requirements.
Provide the customer account, itemized purchase or installation records, model data, and any enrollment or verification information requested by SMECO.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Most mapped HVAC, heat-pump water-heater, thermostat, and connected-control measures have current objective incentive or enrollment paths. A compliant customer is likely to receive the applicable benefit, but the current official pages reviewed do not clearly substantiate the broad high-efficiency-refrigeration mapping.
reviews.evidenceText: SMECO currently provides residential heating and cooling, heat-pump water-heater, smart-thermostat, and connected-device incentives through measure-specific contractor, retailer, claim, or enrollment channels.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SMECO small-business or nonprofit customer with qualifying existing equipment at the project site.
Request and complete the program no-cost energy analysis.
Accept a program-approved project scope, incentive contribution, and customer cost share for qualifying measures.
Complete the approved lighting, refrigeration, or related retrofit through the program process.
Provide access for installation confirmation, final inspection, and any required closeout documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current small-business and nonprofit offering uses a structured energy analysis and approved retrofit scope, with incentives covering a large share of eligible project cost. A qualifying customer that accepts and completes the approved work is likely to receive the program contribution.
reviews.evidenceText: SMECO currently offers eligible small businesses and nonprofits a no-cost energy analysis and incentives for approved retrofits of existing lighting, refrigeration, and other efficiency equipment, followed by project completion verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SMUD residential customer with a new qualifying battery energy-storage system at the service address.
Complete the battery interconnection process and receive permission to operate.
Use a currently eligible battery manufacturer or integration pathway and enroll within the current period after permission to operate.
Move to the required Solar and Storage Rate and authorize the program controls and data access.
Accept the current multi-year participation commitment and pass enrollment and system verification before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current incentive follows published system, interconnection, rate, enrollment, control, and participation requirements rather than competitive scoring. A qualifying newly interconnected battery that enrolls on time is likely to be paid after successful verification, subject to available program funds.
reviews.evidenceText: SMUD currently offers a homeowner battery incentive after permission to operate, timely enrollment, use of an eligible system, transition to the required rate, authorization of program controls, and a multi-year participation commitment.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying SMUD commercial customer with the charging project located in SMUD territory.
Install new qualifying Level 2 or direct-current fast charging equipment that meets the current program and utility requirements.
Submit the PowerClerk application before construction with the customer account, site plan, electrical one-line, charger specifications, costs, and project documentation.
Receive SMUD incentive reservation or project approval before purchasing or constructing the installation.
Use licensed, permitted installation and satisfy applicable metering, inspection, networking, and data requirements.
Submit the final payment request with invoices, permits, photographs, and completion records after installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SMUD provides a current reservation and payment pathway for qualifying commercial Level 2 and fast-charging projects. A fully documented project that receives an advance reservation and completes the approved scope is likely to receive the incentive while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: SMUD currently requires commercial charging applicants to secure an incentive reservation before construction, then complete permitting, installation, inspection, and a documented final payment request.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SMUD business customer with an existing qualifying facility or project in SMUD territory.
Use the applicable Complete Energy Solutions, prescriptive, or custom incentive route for the selected measure.
Complete the required site assessment or submit technical baseline, cost, equipment, and energy-savings documentation.
Obtain required SMUD technical review and preapproval before purchasing or installing equipment, particularly for custom or larger projects.
Complete the approved installation and submit final invoices, equipment records, commissioning information, and access for inspection or savings verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current business portfolio directly supports heat-pump HVAC, heat-pump water heating, refrigeration, induction, and related measures through prescriptive or managed-project pathways. A qualifying project that follows the applicable approval and closeout process is likely to receive the incentive.
reviews.evidenceText: SMUD currently offers business incentives through managed prescriptive and custom pathways that require assessment or technical review, advance approval when applicable, completed installation records, and final verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SMUD residential customer and install the product at a qualifying service address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying heat pump, smart thermostat, heat-pump water heater, appliance, induction product, or other listed measure.
Use a participating contractor or retailer when required for the selected instant or contractor-delivered incentive.
Meet current equipment, efficiency, installation, permit, and replacement requirements.
Submit or complete the measure-specific claim with account, receipt or invoice, model, installation, and photograph or permit records when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SMUD currently offers the mapped household measures through objective point-of-sale, participating-contractor, or post-installation claim channels. A qualifying purchase or installation is likely to receive the listed rebate after measure-specific validation.
reviews.evidenceText: SMUD currently lists residential heating and cooling, water-heating, thermostat, appliance, laundry, and induction incentives with measure-specific retailer, contractor, receipt, model, installation, and permit requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Snohomish County PUD business customer with the project installed at a qualifying service location.
Propose a currently qualifying HVAC, controls, refrigeration, envelope, motor, fan, pump, or custom energy-efficiency measure.
Submit the project application with equipment specifications, costs, baseline information, and savings calculations as applicable.
Receive PUD preapproval before purchasing or installing equipment.
Complete the approved project and provide final invoices, installation records, and access for post-installation inspection or savings verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current business program explicitly supports most mapped HVAC, thermostat, refrigeration, anti-sweat, insulation, fan, and pump measures under mandatory preapproval. A conforming project is likely to be paid, but waste-heat recovery was not expressly identified and requires custom-project confirmation.
reviews.evidenceText: Snohomish County PUD currently lists 2026 business incentives for heat pumps, controls, variable-speed fans and pumps, insulation, refrigeration, and anti-sweat controls and requires project approval before installation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Snohomish County PUD residential customer with the measure installed in a qualifying home.
Purchase and install an active qualifying heat pump, thermostat, duct, water-heating, insulation, air-sealing, or laundry measure.
Use a PUD-registered contractor for contractor-delivered heat-pump, weatherization, or water-heating incentives when required.
Submit any customer-filed product rebate within the current deadline with receipt, model, account, and installation documentation.
Complete applicable permits, inspections, and PUD verification.
Do not rely on a new EV-charger rebate: the official charger offer ended for purchases after December 31, 2025.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Most mapped home-efficiency measures remain available through objective contractor or post-purchase rebate routes, so a compliant active-measure claim is likely. The mapped EV-charger and Level 2 charger opportunity is no longer current because that rebate ended after 2025 purchases.
reviews.evidenceText: Snohomish County PUD currently offers residential heat-pump, thermostat, duct, water-heating, weatherization, and appliance rebates, while its official EV-charger page states that the charger rebate ended for purchases after December 31, 2025.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible SoCalGas non-residential customer with a qualifying natural-gas efficiency project at the service location.
Propose a custom retrofit, retrocommissioning, process, or systems project with measurable gas savings that is not appropriately handled as a standard prescriptive rebate.
Submit baseline, engineering, cost, operating, equipment, and savings documentation for program technical and cost-effectiveness review before installation.
Receive written project approval and an incentive reservation before purchasing, constructing, or installing the measure.
Complete the approved scope and provide final invoices, commissioning records, inspection access, and measurement or savings-verification documentation before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Customized incentives remain an official business pathway, but every project depends on engineering savings, cost-effectiveness, technical eligibility, advance reservation, available funding, and final verification. Award is therefore possible rather than routine, especially while program delivery transitions toward third-party implementation.
reviews.evidenceText: SoCalGas currently advertises customized business incentives, and its latest efficiency report describes the calculated-incentive route for custom retrofit and retrocommissioning projects, with advance review, reservation, implementation, and savings verification.

approvalRequirements: Be the owner, manager, or authorized applicant for an eligible existing multifamily property served by SoCalGas.
Purchase and install a new qualifying natural-gas oven that replaces eligible existing natural-gas equipment and meets the current product specifications.
Complete the purchase and installation within the current 2026 program period.
Submit the signed rebate application with a recent matching SoCalGas bill, paid itemized invoice or receipt, model information, and installation records by the current deadline.
Remain within program limits and permit SoCalGas to inspect or otherwise verify the equipment and installation before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current multifamily application provides a prescriptive rebate route for qualifying natural-gas ovens under objective property, equipment, timing, and documentation rules. A complete timely claim is likely to be paid after review while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: SoCalGas currently provides a 2026 multifamily rebate application covering qualifying natural-gas equipment, including eligible ovens, and requires an existing multifamily property, current utility bill, paid itemized records, timely filing, and possible verification.
